FROM PIXELS TO PERSPECTIVE

What happens when you enter?

  1. Imagine the surroundings. A panorama model can extend a picture into a full surrounding scene. Hidden areas are invented, and details may change.
  2. Wrap the panorama. A 2:1 equirectangular image is placed inside a sphere. You sit at its center and turn the camera.
  3. Look around. Drag or use arrow keys to turn. Scroll to zoom. This is a single viewpoint, not a walkable 3D mesh.

The included panorama was generated with image generation from the public-domain painting. New panorama generation is not built into this website. The linked external model is an optional free route with variable availability; our anonymous test returned an error.

Ordinary photo uploads use Depth Anything V2 Small locally to estimate a textured depth surface. That mode supports small viewpoint changes, but cannot invent a whole surrounding scene. Panorama imports are displayed locally too.

The example painting is public domain, supplied by the Art Institute of Chicago.
